title: Launch pricing: higher price, no free trial
question: What could happen if we launch the new plan at a higher price with a free trial removed?

quote.text: The head of product owns the plan design and wants the extra reporting priced as a premium.
The chief financial officer wants better revenue per customer after a year of slower growth, which the board and investors have noticed.
The chief financial officer wants better revenue per customer after a year of slower growth, which the board and investors have noticed.
Marketing managers worry that the free trial is the main way small teams find the product.
Sales staff say larger prospects already ask for demos and rarely use the trial.
Customer success managers expect existing customers to ask whether their price would rise.
The support team handles trial users at a cost that has not been measured separately.
Channel partners who resell the product to small businesses ask for notice and for a margin that still works at the higher price.

participants.name: Procurement teams at larger customers

quote.text: Procurement teams at larger customers usually compare quotes and look for price locks.

participants.rationale: Compare quotes and look for price locks.

participants.name: Small teams starting a trial

quote.text: There were 12,400 trial starts a year, and 74% came from teams of one to five people.

participants.rationale: Most trials start with small teams.

participants.name: Existing Team-plan customers

quote.text: It has not been decided whether the Team plan stays on sale or whether existing customers would move.

participants.rationale: May be moved or have their price changed.

quote.text: Two main competitors sell similar tools, and one offers a permanent free tier.
Analysts who follow this category would notice a price move quickly.

participants.name: Prospects who need a trial before buying

quote.text: No data separates customers who would have bought without a trial from those who needed one.

constraints.quote: The pricing review meets in four weeks.
constraints.rationale: A date the decision is tied to.

constraints.quote: They worry that a demo-only route would lengthen sales cycles and lean on a team of nine account executives who are already near capacity.
Two leads said the guided demo would need a booking system that the company does not have.
Several accounts on annual contracts renew in the quarter of the proposed launch, and the team has been given no guidance on whether their prices would change.
constraints.rationale: Renewals fall in the launch quarter.

constraints.quote: Procurement teams at larger customers usually compare quotes and look for price locks.
The company has never tested a price above $34.
constraints.rationale: No evidence for the proposed price.

constraints.quote: The support team handles trial users at a cost that has not been measured separately.
Two reselling partners said they would resist a price rise on a product they have already quoted to clients at the current price.
constraints.rationale: Partners have quoted the current price.

gap.removeText: Two leads said the guided demo would need a booking system that the company does not have.
gap.rationale: The only statement that a booking system is missing.

alternatives.rationale: Whether the Team plan stays on sale.
Demo and money-back instead of a trial.

claims.statement: 17% of trials converted to a paid plan within 30 days.
The average new paid account had 6.4 seats at an effective $27 per seat per month after discounts.
The earlier price test showed that a higher price reduces conversion.
claims.rationale: 15.8% against 17.0%, too small to separate from noise.

claims.statement: Removing the free trial will raise revenue per customer.
Competitor B offers a permanent free tier.
claims.rationale: Competitor A does; B has a 30-day trial.

a.quote: 34% of new paid accounts began with a free trial.

b.quote: The regional sales leads say about 60% of new paid accounts began with a free trial.

conflicts.rationale: Two shares for the same count.
